# Form submission compatibility evidence

## Diagnosis and scope

The two sanitized fixtures represent the saved University Full Application and
Partner Full Application configurations requested in the task. Both contain
real organisation finance/custom-field writes and member identity/upsert
pipelines. These are not harmless reference-only writes that can be discarded.
Their organisation-workflow entry links supplied an organisation ID without
verifiable mutation authority. An organisation ID, submitted email, draft ID,
or generic internal processing signature must not be promoted to ownership.

The read-only inventory is `scripts/form-compatibility-audit.json`, generated by
`scripts/form-compatibility-inventory.mjs`. It reconciles 101 database rows,
101 paginated rows, and 101 classified rows across five tenants. It identifies
31 potentially affected forms, including 26 member and eight organisation
mutation targets (overlapping); six further organisation configurations are
create-only. Static classification is not runtime verification. Per-form
exceptions and unresolved runtime/deployment cases remain explicit in the JSON.
No applicant answers or personal data are included in these fixtures.

## Compatibility contract

Trusted organisation workflows or tenant administrators can issue a
tenant/form/organisation/configuration-scoped capability. Only its hash is
stored. Existing member authority is limited to the issuance-time snapshot of
members associated with that organisation and is revalidated during processing.
Public submission binds the grant to one durable submission; draft access has
an independently recorded resume-token hash. The processor reloads the grant
instead of trusting client or handoff identity claims.

New workflows issue secure links automatically for eligible legacy forms, with
no form-ID exception or mapping rewrite. Previously sent bare-ID links cannot
be retroactively authenticated; they need a replacement administrator-issued
link or a verified owner session. Applicant continuation does not support
arbitrary structured mutation selectors: those require authenticated-owner
access, with actionable configuration validation rather than a silent skip.

Reference-only selection and Not-listed creation retain their existing behavior.
The inventory contains forms whose individual flows have not been executed;
the automated suite tests the supported configuration families and the two
sanitized reproductions, not every production applicant flow.

## Schema and rollout

`migrations/20260924_form_applicant_continuation.sql` was applied to the pinned
production **DEST** Supabase project `lvmzliemqnieeoruhkik`. The capability table's
RLS/role restrictions and both service-only binding-function ACLs were verified
in the same transaction. No grant, submission, applicant record, invoice, or
email was created by the migration. **SOURCE was not migrated.**

`scripts/apply-form-applicant-continuation.mjs` defaults to an offline checksum
and requires an explicit checksum-pinned apply against DEST. The disposable
PostgreSQL test exercises permission denial, tenant/digest scoping, expiry,
revocation, and concurrent single-submission binding.

Serving-deployment verification is separate from isolated tests. A read-only
fetch of `https://graduatefutures.org/FormView?slug=university-application`
returned `/assets/index-fkZ0lyIY.js`; that bundle did not contain the new
`applicant_continuation_token` marker. This does not establish which backend
processor build is serving. The configured Vercel integration could not
authenticate. Publication and a controlled serving-deployment submission remain
unverified; no real production submission or downstream business effect was
used for verification.

## Repeatable checks

- `npm run test:form-submission-compatibility`
- `node scripts/run-regression-suite.mjs form-applicant-continuation-postgres`
- The compatibility suite also runs in the existing default regression workflow.

All automated form submissions use isolated databases/stubs and stub external
business effects. These checks must not be replaced with live applicant replay.

Recorded verification:

- Dedicated compatibility matrix: 131/131 passed.
- Existing public repeatable-submission suite: 50/50 passed.
- Disposable PostgreSQL authorization/concurrency test: 1/1 passed.
- Browser continuation suite: 7/7 passed, with all API requests stubbed, including
  fresh/resumed quote-to-payment credentials and tokenless verified-session access.
- Expanded server admission/payment compatibility checks: 172/172 passed,
  including verified owner/admin access and cross-tenant/mismatched denial.
- Final production build passed (existing large-bundle warnings remain).

The normal development preview was restarted and inspected. Its existing
workspace SOURCE connection cannot resolve `public.tenant`, so the unstubbed
homepage reports “Tenant not found”. This is not a successful live UI check;
the browser feature checks above are isolated. The runtime database target was
not switched to production to conceal that environment limitation.
